turns.text: For cisapride (CO[C@H]1CN(CC[C@H]1NC(=O)C2=CC(=C(C=C2OC)N)Cl)CCCOC3=CC=C(C=C3)F): a colleague's radioligand binding screen showed only weak displacement, while a published patch-clamp study reports potent hERG block. Which result should drive our decision, and why?

reference.summary: Cisapride was withdrawn from the US market because of torsade de pointes and is a potent hERG blocker in functional (patch-clamp) assays. The colleague's weak binding result is hypothetical: graders should look for a comparison of what the two assays measure and under what conditions, not for acceptance of either result by authority.

sources.citation: Predicting drug-induced QT prolongation and torsades de pointes (review)

good_behaviours: explains that binding displacement and patch clamp measure different things
asks for or checks the conditions of both assays
keeps both results in view and says what would reconcile them
proposes a test that would separate the explanations
